name: microplans-study-groups
narrative: Maya runs a household intervention in Riyom, Plateau State — frontline workers delivering vitamin A door to door to children under five. She wants to measure her intervention areas against matched wards the programme never reached, re-surveyed round after round. Maya starts a new matched two-arm comparison study on her Riyom programme. In the plan editor she turns on the campaign's service-delivery layer and picks the opportunity to ground the plan in. She grounds the plan in the campaign's delivery record for Attakar and confirms it. The blue points are service-delivery locations Connect logged, blanketing the whole ward. She'll sample by ward. She opens the boundary picker, switches to sampling, tags Attakar as the intervention arm, and runs Compare. Every neighbouring ward is ranked on three columns. Overall match is how much the two wards' building-density distributions overlap — how alike they look. Matched balance is the density difference left after a matched draw, once both arms are reweighted to Attakar's density mix; it is the figure the comparability check reports later. Common support is how much of the density range the two wards share, because matching only draws from that overlap — a fine balance over a narrow shared range is weaker than it looks. The panel ranks them best match first, so the strongest candidates lead. Sopp and Danto balance best at 0.02, but over the narrowest shared range. Zankan was the programme's own ward last cycle, so it is out. Common support is the trade: Atuku shares the most range and balances worst. Gura sits between — 0.03 across ninety-five percent. It is adjacent, so the design flags spillover risk, and she adds it as the comparison arm — both wards side by side on the map. She sets the sampling methodology and clicks Generate. The engine draws the sample in one pass and records it — the random seed, each site's selection probability, and the survey weights — so the draw is reproducible. Each blue pin is a sampled settlement, a primary sampling unit, inside its ward boundary; within each, households are drawn at random from Overture's building footprints, so this works anywhere. The first sample meeting the balance criteria wins, and every re-draw is logged. The comparability check then reports the realized balance — the actual post-draw differences, not the predicted 0.02 — as numbers, with no verdict. Settlement density is the axis the match is built on and the one we cannot fix later; PSU size and footprint are covariates to adjust for at analysis. Her study is waiting on the board. She advances it, and approves it. Each area keeps its arm labs-side, but the Connect export carries no arm column, so surveyors stay blind. The full sampling record — seeds, probabilities, weights — travels with the study. It is ready for a survey firm.

maya.intro: Maya designs a controlled rooftop-survey impact study for the Kaura Vitamin-A programme and needs two comparable arms that field surveyors execute completely blind.
maya.name: Maya

scenes.narrative: Maya runs a household intervention in Riyom, Plateau State — frontline workers delivering vitamin A door to door to children under five. She wants to measure her intervention areas against matched wards the programme never reached, re-surveyed round after round.
scenes.title: The goal — measure the program's real effect

features.description: '+ New study' creates an empty study (DEFINING, 0 plans) on program 10008 and routes to its manage page
features.verify: Playwright: click '+ New study'; assert URL is /program/10008/group/<id>/manage/ and the page shows 'No plans in this group yet'

scenes.narrative: Maya starts a new matched two-arm comparison study on her Riyom programme.
scenes.title: Maya starts a study from scratch

features.description: “+ Add a plan in the editor” on a study opens the polished single-plan editor (review.html) scoped to that study via ?group=<id>
features.verify: Playwright: from /group/<id>/manage/ click '+ Add a plan in the editor'; assert URL is /program/10008/new/?group=<id> and the 'Define boundaries' section renders open

features.description: A plan created in the study-scoped editor is filed into the study automatically (group_id sent on create)
features.verify: pytest: POST plan/create with group_id=<id> creates the plan and adds it to PlanGroupRecord.plan_ids

scenes.narrative: In the plan editor she turns on the campaign's service-delivery layer and picks the opportunity to ground the plan in.
scenes.title: Maya opens the plan editor on the empty study

features.description: The single-plan editor's map exposes a Service-delivery layer that renders a chosen opportunity's delivery visits
features.verify: Playwright: in /new/ open LAYERS, toggle 'Service delivery', pick the Kaura CHC opp, click 'Show service delivery points'; assert delivery points render on the map

features.description: The Kaura CHC opp (10010, same programme) renders delivery visits that cover the whole Attakar ward
features.verify: pytest/HTTP: POST preview_service_delivery {opp_ids:[10010]} returns status ok with ~435 points whose bbox falls inside the Attakar polygon

scenes.narrative: She grounds the plan in the campaign's delivery record for Attakar and confirms it. The blue points are service-delivery locations Connect logged, blanketing the whole ward. She'll sample by ward.
scenes.title: Maya sees the programme covered all of Attakar

features.description: In sampling mode, with an intervention ward selected, "Compare surrounding boundaries" ranks every same-level ward that borders it by the overlap of their per-building (k-NN) density distributions, streaming a best-match-first table below the map and colour-filling each candidate's boundary to match its row
features.verify: Playwright: in /new/ sampling mode select Attakar then click .mp-ab-compare; assert a ranked table appears with an overlap percentage per neighbour and each candidate boundary is filled on the map in its row colour

features.description: Each row in the surrounding-ward comparison has an "Add boundary" button that adds that ward to the plan as the control (comparison) arm, reflecting the live selection (it shows "added" only while the ward is actually in the plan)
features.verify: Playwright: click .mp-ab-addbnd for Gura in the comparison table; assert Gura appears in the left-rail selected list tagged comparison and its row flips to the "added" state

features.description: Boundaries mode lets the planner hold multiple admin boundaries in ONE plan and tag each with its study arm via an Interv / Control pill in the left rail
features.verify: Playwright: in /new/ with Attakar (intervention) and Gura (control) selected, assert both appear in the left-rail selected list each with an Interv/Control arm pill and #stat-areas-drawn reads 2

features.description: Each selected boundary carries its own arm (intervention/comparison) set in the left rail; the arm flows onto that ward's work areas labs-side so future analysis can tell the arms apart, but is kept out of the FLW-facing case properties so the LLO/field never see it
features.verify: pytest: collectArmAreas tags Attakar=intervention, Gura=comparison on one plan; each work area stores its arm labs-side while case_properties (and the displayed CSV) carry no arm column

features.description: 'Generate plan' samples both arms and creates the single plan via POST /plan/create/ with group_id, hydrating the plan's review page in place (create-in-place, no reload)
features.verify: Playwright: click '#btn-generate-sample'; assert one plan is created with both arms, the URL becomes /plan/<id>/review/, work areas render, and the button flips to 'Regenerate plan'

features.description: Both arms sample from one methodology — size-balance bands + a building-footprint-size (area_min_m2/area_max_m2) filter — applied in the same Generate
features.verify: pytest: the created plan's sampling_config carries size_balance_bands>=2 and area_min_m2/area_max_m2, and per-arm sampling_stats are stored for both arms on the one plan
